person_note: The diagnostic event passages repeatedly use an external narrator who enters characters' private memories, realizations, grief, and ignorance, including access to more than one character's mind. Scholarly whole-book analysis and three explicit reference sources independently identify third-person or third-person omniscient narration, with focal shifts that remain within third person. Apparent first- and second-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue, universal aphorisms, or the character thought embedded in q02362; none constitutes an autonomous base section. The main limitation is that several popular quotations are clipped or too short to diagnose independently, but they do not create credible contrary evidence.
